source.title: MetaPerturb: Transferable Regularizer for Heterogeneous Tasks and Architectures
source.authors: Jeongun Ryu; Jaewoong Shin; Haebeom Lee; Sung Ju Hwang

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the paper and supplementary file.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a learned regularizer on heterogeneous image datasets and convolutional architectures, reporting held-out accuracy; it does not test the claim versions’ specified mechanisms.
record.gate_note: Reports held-out accuracy comparisons for MetaPerturb and baselines. Optimizer, batch size, model size, and architecture settings are not swept to test their effects on the training–test gap.
record.test_reason: The MetaPerturb comparisons do not test a listed version, but the study's own DropBlock-versus-Base results bear on V6: DropBlock explicitly drops contiguous groups of units in convolutional classifiers. This tests a structured dropout variant in additional settings, rather than standard independent-unit dropout.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase accurately describes the authors' conclusion: a lightweight meta-learned perturbation transfers across image tasks and convolutional architectures and improves generalization over baselines in most tested settings. It should remain attributed to the authors: Table 1 does not show superiority over every baseline on every dataset.
record.recipe_differences: Meta-learns a shared latent-feature perturbation and evaluates held-out accuracy across image tasks and convolutional networks; does not use the original claim’s interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported performance varies across datasets and target architectures; the study also reports that homogeneous source-task splits degrade performance relative to heterogeneous splits.

fits_no_version.finding: MetaPerturb improves mean test accuracy over Base across the recorded datasets and convolutional architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A transferred, meta-learned feature perturbation can improve image-classification accuracy across heterogeneous tasks and convolutional architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 8 visually shows flatter training-loss surfaces for MetaPerturb and Manifold Mixup than for the displayed baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some regularizers yielding better test accuracy also produce visually flatter loss landscapes in the CUB/ResNet20 comparison; this does not establish V7's specific measure or gap-ranking claim.

record.problems: The reported comparisons focus on test accuracy rather than the training–test gap. MetaPerturb is selected using a validation set; no random-label condition or fully connected architecture comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Other baseline method values, test cross-entropy, calibration, robustness, ablation and supplementary ECE results were left out because they do not test a listed claim version or add a distinct finding needed for the proposed claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under controlled tuning; using Adam throughout is not a comparison.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Standard independent-unit dropout, fully connected classifiers, a controlled training-set-size comparison, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with measured generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Identifying memorized examples and comparing their removal with random removal.

missing.what: Add DropBlock-versus-Base accuracy rows linked to V6. Table 1 Base→DropBlock: STL10 66.78±0.59→68.51±0.67; s-CIFAR100 31.79±0.24→32.74±0.36; Dogs 34.65±1.05→34.59±0.87; Cars 44.34±1.10→45.11±1.47; Aircraft 59.23±0.95→59.76±1.38; CUB 30.63±0.66→30.55±0.26. These are structured-dropout comparisons with weight decay and augmentation retained.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooked its own structured-dropout baseline evidence. Although rows_left_out broadly declares baseline values omitted, the DropBlock results are identified here because the verdict rules require missing entries when a tested version is absent from the rows. Information Dropout and MetaPerturb use learned multiplicative perturbations and are not treated as direct tests of ordinary unit-dropping dropout. Reported uncertainties are standard deviations across five runs; small mean differences are not independently established as statistically significant.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparisons.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects, small training sets, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measured against the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: DropBlock on STL10 with ResNet20, and on small-SVHN with ResNet20, ResNet44 and WRN-28-2; weight decay and augmentation retained.
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict from omitted DropBlock comparisons: accuracy rises from 66.78 to 68.51, 87.96 to 89.43, 88.94 to 90.14, and 88.95 to 90.55, respectively; no existing row records these contrasts.
relationships.display_finding: Structured dropout reportedly increased accuracy across these comparisons with augmentation and weight decay retained, but the comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.condition: DropBlock on STL10 with ResNet20, and on small-SVHN with ResNet20, ResNet44 and WRN-28-2; weight decay and augmentation retained.
source_check.reason: Tables 1–2 give Base→DropBlock accuracy of 66.78→68.51, 87.96→89.43, 88.94→90.14 and 88.95→90.55, respectively; these support beneficial regimes.

relationships.condition: DropBlock on s-CIFAR100, Cars and Aircraft with ResNet20, and small-SVHN with Conv4, Conv6 and VGG9.
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict: mean accuracy gains are only 0.95, 0.77, 0.53, 0.36, 0.08 and 0.24 percentage points, respectively, showing weaker benefits; no existing row records these contrasts.
relationships.display_finding: DropBlock reportedly produced small mean accuracy gains across these tasks and architectures. These comparisons have not been independently checked.

source_check.notes: No rows were listed for checking; the verdicts rely on unextracted comparisons in Tables 1–2, reported as means and standard deviations over five runs. DropBlock is structured dropout; the authors' MetaPerturb conclusion is accurately paraphrased with the stated qualification.
